headline: Oil fell nearly 8%, one of its biggest drops of the US–Iran war, after Iran said its supreme leader backed peace talks. The dollar slipped as inflation fears eased; the Swiss franc gained most.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar index slipped about 0.3% to near 101.7, touching a one-month low, as oil's slide eased fears of US inflation. A strong US factory survey barely helped, and bets on a December Federal Reserve hike held near three in four.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: High oil from the US–Iran war has kept US inflation well above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal. The Fed held rates on October 28 with two officials voting to hike, and others have since called for more hikes. What changed: The ISM survey of US factories rose to 55.5 in October, beating forecasts, with output the strongest in almost five years. But the prices factories pay rose a little more slowly, and oil fell nearly 8% after Iran signalled support for peace talks. The dollar index fell to about 101.7 and the 10-year Treasury yield eased to near 4.90%. What it means: Strong growth backs the Fed officials who want higher rates, but cheaper oil takes away part of the reason to hurry. The dollar now hinges on how much pressure the Fed is under, and this week's jobs and services figures will show that.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US midterm elections on Tuesday, with results overnight, US job openings at 9:00 AM CT Tuesday, the ISM services survey at 9:00 AM CT Wednesday, and the October jobs report at 7:30 AM CT Friday. The next Fed decision is December 9.

scenarios.base: Midterms pass without a market shock and oil holds near $105; the index stays between about 101.2 and 102.2.
scenarios.bull: Strong job openings or services figures, or oil rebounding on a stalled deal, lift the index above 102.2.
scenarios.bear: Another big leg down in oil or weak US data trims December hike bets; the index falls below 101.2.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro rose about 0.3% to near $1.119, after touching $1.124 in Europe, as cheaper oil eased the energy bill for a region that imports most of its fuel. It gave back part of the gain in New York.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy costs have pushed euro-area inflation well above the European Central Bank's 2% goal, and the ECB held rates on October 29 while pointing to a hike in December. France's debt worries, with two rating firms now on negative outlook, keep a weight on the euro. What changed: Oil's fall did most of the work, cutting the cost of the region's energy imports. Final figures showed euro-area factories still growing in October at 52.7, though their costs rose at the fastest pace since May. The euro peaked near $1.124 in Europe, then slipped back as the dollar steadied. What it means: Cheaper energy helps the euro, but it also eases price pressure, which could soften the case for an ECB hike. The question for the euro is whether Wednesday's inflation figure keeps the December hike firmly in place.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: France's parliament votes on the revenue part of its budget on Tuesday, euro-area inflation for October at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday (forecast 4.0%, September 3.8%), and a speech by ECB President Christine Lagarde at noon CT Thursday.

scenarios.base: Inflation near forecast; the euro stays between about $1.112 and $1.126.
scenarios.bull: Inflation of 4.2% or more, or oil falling further, lifts the euro above $1.126.
scenarios.bear: A soft inflation figure or fresh French budget trouble sends the euro below $1.112.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound rose about 0.2% to near $1.341 as UK factories had their best month for output in two years. Markets still see a Bank of England hike on Thursday, November 5, as all but certain.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, its highest in about a year, driven by energy and fuel. The Bank of England is widely expected to raise rates on Thursday for the first time since 2023. What changed: The UK factory survey rose to 52.8 in October, a five-month high, with output growing at its fastest pace in 25 months and factory prices climbing faster. The pound touched $1.345 before easing, and held near its strongest against the euro in about 19 months. What it means: Firm demand and rising costs make Thursday's hike easier to justify. With the hike nearly fully priced, the pound will move on whether the bank hints at a second one in December.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of England decision and its Monetary Policy Report at 6:00 AM CT Thursday, November 5. Before that, UK services surveys midweek and the US midterms on Tuesday.

scenarios.base: A hike Thursday with an open door to more; the pound stays between about $1.334 and $1.348.
scenarios.bull: A hike plus a clear hint of December; the pound rises above $1.348.
scenarios.bear: A hike framed as the last for now, or a split vote leaning toward caution; the pound falls below $1.334.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The dollar edged up about 0.2% to near ¥157.9 after failing to break ¥158 in Tokyo. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama repeated that Tokyo is ready to act against sharp moves, and said US–Japan currency cooperation will not change after the midterms.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japanese rates are far below those of other major economies, and high oil costs Japan money, which has kept the yen weak. The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% on October 30 but said underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal, pointing toward a December hike. What changed: Oil's big fall helps Japan, which imports almost all its energy, but the yen barely gained. US yields eased only slightly, so the wide rate gap still dominated. Katayama's warning kept a lid on the dollar near ¥158. What it means: The yen needs a clear Bank of Japan signal or a bigger drop in US yields to gain much ground. Tokyo's warnings limit how weak it gets, so the question is whether US data this week widens or narrows the rate gap.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US midterms on Tuesday, the US jobs report at 7:30 AM CT Friday, and a speech by Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda at 10:00 AM CT Friday. The next Bank of Japan decision is December 18.
numbers: Bank of Japan rate 1.25%; December hike ~80% priced

scenarios.bull: Strong US data lifts yields; the dollar rises above ¥158.8, likely drawing louder warnings from Tokyo.
scenarios.bear: A share slide or a hint from Ueda about December; the dollar falls below ¥156.8.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc was the strongest major currency, with the dollar down about 0.6% to near 0.819 francs. Cheaper oil and a slide in US tech shares drew money into the franc before Swiss inflation figures early Tuesday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Swiss inflation is low, so the Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero and has said it is less ready to fight a weaker franc. The franc mostly moves on the global mood. What changed: High oil had dulled the franc's appeal as a safe place to park money, because energy shocks hurt Europe. Oil's sharp fall eased that, and a drop of about 1% in the Nasdaq index of US tech shares gave investors a reason to seek safety. What it means: The franc is again trading as a shelter, which can lift it quickly. A soft inflation reading on Tuesday would keep talk of a Swiss rate cut alive and could cap the gain.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Swiss inflation for October at 1:30 AM CT Tuesday (forecast 0.0% on the month), and a speech by Swiss National Bank Chairman Martin Schlegel at 6:40 AM CT Thursday. The next decision is December 10.
numbers: USD/CHF ~0.8185 (−0.61%), the biggest move among majors

scenarios.bull: Calm markets and a soft Swiss inflation reading; the dollar rises above 0.825 francs.
scenarios.bear: A deeper share slide or a new Gulf scare; the dollar falls below 0.812 francs.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie fell about 0.5% to just under 70 US cents, the weakest major, before the Reserve Bank of Australia decision at 9:30 PM CT tonight. Markets put a hike to 4.85% at roughly 80%.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Australian inflation ran hotter than the Reserve Bank of Australia expected, and the bank has raised rates four times this year. A weakening job market is the main drag. What changed: The Aussie lagged even as the dollar slipped, as oil's slide took some shine off Australia's energy exports and traders trimmed bets before the decision. Pricing for a hike held near 80%, with most economists expecting one. What it means: The hike itself is mostly expected, so the Aussie will move on what Governor Michele Bullock signals about more. In September her press conference sounded softer than the written statement and faded an early gain, so the tone matters as much as the decision.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the RBA decision and new forecasts at 9:30 PM CT tonight, then Governor Michele Bullock's press conference at 10:30 PM CT. The US jobs report follows at 7:30 AM CT Friday.

scenarios.base: A hike with a cautious tone; the Aussie stays between about 69.4 and 70.6 cents.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a clear hint of more; the Aussie rises above 70.6 cents.
scenarios.bear: A surprise hold or a hint this is the last hike; the Aussie falls below 69.4 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie held up well, with the US dollar up only about 0.2% to near 1.397, even as US crude fell more than 7% to about $96.50. Hopes for a US–Canada trade deal helped cushion the hit.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Bank of Canada raised rates to 2.50% on October 28 as energy lifted inflation, but the economy has not grown since June. High oil prices have helped the loonie. What changed: US crude settled below $100 for the first time in weeks, which would normally weigh on the currency of a big oil exporter. The loonie lost little, helped by President Donald Trump's Sunday remark that a trade deal with Canada is very close, though no terms have been given. What it means: Oil is a smaller prop than it was, so the loonie leans more on trade hopes and on the Bank of Canada. The question is whether a signed deal arrives before oil's fall goes further.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem speaks at 10:00 AM CT Tuesday and 9:30 AM CT Thursday, Canada's federal budget lands at 3:00 PM CT Thursday, and Canada's October jobs report comes at 7:30 AM CT Friday.
numbers: December Bank of Canada hike ~45% priced

scenarios.bull: A signed trade deal or oil rebounding above $100; the US dollar falls below 1.390 loonies.
scenarios.bear: WTI sliding toward $90 on a firm Iran deal; the US dollar rises above 1.405 loonies.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi slipped about 0.2% to near 56.2 US cents before New Zealand's job figures at 3:45 PM CT Tuesday. A general election follows on Saturday, November 7.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised markets by holding at 2.75% on October 28, though all its members said more tightening is likely. Unemployment sits near a decade high. What changed: Little New Zealand news. The kiwi drifted lower with the Aussie before the Australian rate decision tonight, and election nerves kept buyers cautious. What it means: The job figures are the next big clue for a December hike: strong hiring would firm it up and support the kiwi, weak hiring would push it back. The election adds a second source of swings at the end of the week.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the RBA decision at 9:30 PM CT tonight, New Zealand's job figures for July to September at 3:45 PM CT Tuesday (forecast: jobs +0.4%, unemployment 5.5%), then the election on Saturday, November 7. The next RBNZ decision is December 9.
numbers: RBNZ rate 2.75%; December hike leaning likely

scenarios.bull: Unemployment of 5.4% or lower firms up a December hike; the kiwi rises above 56.8 cents.
scenarios.bear: Unemployment of 5.7% or higher, or election worries; the kiwi falls below 55.6 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent settled down 7.6% at about $104.80 a barrel and US crude fell below $100, one of the biggest one-day drops of the US–Iran war. Iran's president said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has given the government powers to pursue peace talks.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The US–Iran war and a US blockade of Iranian ports have kept oil high, with Iran keeping the Strait of Hormuz, the route for about a fifth of the world's oil, mostly shut. What changed: Prices fell about 3% overnight on talks in Qatar, then the drop roughly doubled after President Masoud Pezeshkian said the Supreme Leader backs a negotiated end to the war. Iran's negotiators left Doha with a draft deal circulating, and President Donald Trump said Iran wants to make a deal. But Iran still says Hormuz will not reopen until the US blockade ends, and ships are still being hit in the Gulf. What it means: Markets are pricing hope, not a signed deal, and stockpiles are already low, so a setback could reverse the drop quickly. Cheaper oil eases inflation pressure worldwide, helps importers such as Japan and the euro area, and weighs on exporters such as Canada.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any US answer to the Doha draft, the US midterm elections on Tuesday after earlier reports of possible US strikes once the vote is over, and US crude stock figures on Tuesday afternoon and at 9:30 AM CT Wednesday.

scenarios.base: Talks drag on with no deal and no strike; Brent stays between about $100 and $110.
scenarios.bull: Talks stall, the US rejects the draft, or a big attack hits Gulf supply; Brent rises above $110.
scenarios.bear: A plan to reopen Hormuz is agreed; Brent falls below $100.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold rose about 1.7% to near $3,941 an ounce after touching $3,970. A softer dollar and lower US yields helped it climb off last week's one-year low.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold fell almost 7% in October, hit by bets that central banks will keep raising rates to fight energy-driven inflation, and by selling to cover stock losses during a tech slide. What changed: Oil's sharp fall eased inflation fears and pulled US yields lower, which makes gold, which pays no interest, more attractive. A weaker dollar added a lift. Bets on a December Fed hike held near three in four. What it means: This looks like a recovery from forced selling, not a turn, because the chance of a Fed hike has not gone away. The question for gold is whether this week's US jobs and services figures push those hike bets up or down.
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the US midterms on Tuesday, the ISM services survey at 9:00 AM CT Wednesday, and the US jobs report at 7:30 AM CT Friday.

scenarios.bear: Strong US data lifts hike bets; gold falls below $3,880.

calls.text: Dollar index near 101.7 with no major US data left today: if oil keeps falling, it slips toward 101.5 by the close; an oil rebound lifts it back toward 101.8
calls.note: Oil eased only slightly, yet the dollar index rose to about 102.0 by the close, past both levels, as investors favoured the dollar before the Fed.

calls.text: Pound near $1.337 before Wednesday's UK Budget: with no UK data, it stays between $1.333 and $1.341 by the close; a Budget leak on borrowing moves it out of that range
calls.note: With no UK data and no Budget leak, the pound ended near $1.3346, inside the range.

calls.text: Brent near $114 after Aramco cleared its Dhahran headquarters: a Houthi hit that cuts Saudi output lifts Brent past its May highs and supports the loonie; a quiet weekend lets it ease toward $110
calls.note: Both happened in turn: Houthi attacks lifted Brent to about $117 on Friday without a confirmed cut to Saudi output, then a quiet weekend and talks in Tehran took it to about $110 by Monday.

calls.text: Canada retail sales Fri 7:30 AM CT (about +1.3% expected for August): a strong rebound lifts bets on Bank of Canada hikes beyond October 28; a miss keeps it to one
calls.note: Sales rose 1.2%, a touch under the 1.3% expected, so neither a strong beat nor a miss; Bank of Canada hike pricing for October 28 stayed near 75–80%.

calls.text: Brent near $112 after the Iran strike-plan report: a confirmed hit on Gulf oil output or a US move toward strikes pushes it above the $112.68 high and lifts the yen and franc; an official denial lets it slip toward $108 by the close
calls.note: Brent did top the high, to about $113, and the yen and franc gained, but without a confirmed hit or an official US move: the report alone and Iran's tanker claims did it.

calls.text: Euro-area consumer confidence 9:00 AM CT (about −17 expected) with France's gap over Germany at its widest since 2011: a weaker reading keeps the euro under $1.12; a steady one lets it recover
calls.note: The reading was weaker (−17.9), yet the euro recovered to about $1.1218 as US yields fell, so the bond rally outweighed the survey.

calls.text: US bond rally on war fears: if the 10-year yield stays near 5.05% into the close, the yen holds its gains near ¥157; if yields rebound on the strong claims figure, the dollar climbs back toward ¥158
calls.note: Yields did not rebound; they fell further, to about 4.95%, on a tech sell-off, and the yen extended its gains to about ¥156.85.

calls.text: US 10-year yield below 5% after the tech sell-off: if Asian and European stocks keep falling overnight, the yen pushes toward ¥156 and the dollar index slips under 101.5; a rebound in stocks lifts yields and the dollar back toward ¥157.5
calls.note: Asian stocks kept falling (Nikkei −1.3%) and the dollar dipped to about ¥156.3, but steadied near ¥156.9 by 12:40 AM CT; the dollar index held at about 101.5 rather than slipping under it.

calls.text: Euro-area flash business surveys Fri 3:00 AM CT (manufacturing ~52.7, services ~52.6 expected), hours before Moody's on France: misses keep the euro near $1.12; beats firm December ECB hike bets and lift it
calls.note: The surveys missed (euro-area composite 51.9, France back in contraction at 48.4), and the euro stayed near $1.12.

calls.text: US flash PMIs Fri 8:45 AM CT (services ~58.0 expected) and Michigan inflation expectations 9:00 AM CT: firm readings lift yields back toward 5% and steady the dollar; soft ones extend the bond rally
calls.note: The surveys were firm on prices and the Michigan inflation outlook ticked up; the 10-year yield rose back to about 5.00% and the dollar index firmed to about 101.8 on Friday.

calls.text: SNB policy summary 2:30 AM CT: worry about a strong franc keeps December cut bets alive and caps the franc; a calmer tone lets it firm
calls.note: Calmer tone: the bank dropped its stronger readiness to intervene and gave no December cut signal. The franc firmed slightly, with the dollar near 0.823, and hit a three-month high against the euro.

calls.text: Saudi departure order: widening across the Gulf or a hit on Saudi output puts Brent well above $110 and lifts the dollar and loonie; staying contained lets oil drift
calls.note: Brent did climb well above $110 (about $113 by the close), but on reports of US–Israeli strike plans and Iranian tanker claims, not a wider departure order. The loonie edged up; the dollar slipped.

calls.text: UK retail sales Fri 1:00 AM CT (−0.2% expected): a strong print lifts December hike bets and the pound; a weak one trims both
calls.note: Sales fell 0.4%, worse than expected, yet the pound reached its strongest against the euro since May 2025 on Friday as a November Bank of England hike stayed near certain.

calls.text: US jobless claims Thu 7:30 AM CT (about 200,000 expected): staying low keeps the Fed's December hike near 90%; a jump trims it and weighs on the dollar
calls.note: Claims stayed low at 194,000 (200,000 expected), near their lowest in decades. December hike bets held near 90% (CME FedWatch, Oct 21); a sharp bond rally later still pulled the dollar lower.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
calls.note: The Bank of Canada hiked as priced, and the loonie barely moved on the day.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
